steps.player: Tell me about the Inferno.

steps.npc: TzHaar are born from eggs incubated in lava pools. When hatched, we retain memories. Memories and knowledge passed on from ancestors who returned to the lava.
When TzHaar hatch, some memories are lost. Those about earliest ancestors are not retained. We experiment.
This here was once our largest birthing pool. We use it for experiment. We increased the depth at which eggs are incubated. Over time, newly hatched TzHaar had more memories of lost history!
But we kept pushing. We wanted answers, but we went too deep.
Eventually the pool collapsed into a sinkhole. At the bottom we found some sort of ancient incubation chamber, from before earliest memories. We now call it the Inferno.
We decide to experiment more. We take eggs from creatures in Fight Cave and incubate them down there.
When eggs hatched, we see that it was not good decision. They were bigger and stronger, and fought each other for dominance.

steps.text: If the player has sacrificed a fire cape:

steps.npc: Instead of knowledge, we now have chamber of dangerous creatures, and they're not alone. Another being lives in the Inferno, one more powerful than any TzHaar.
We do not know where he came from. All we know is that TzKal-Zuk is hungry. Hungry for memories, memories beyond the Inferno.
We think his goal is the city itself. Lots of TzHaar memories here for him. Luckily, he is trapped in prison down there, and we are keeping him at bay by offering sacrifices.

steps.text: If the player has not yet beaten the Inferno:

steps.npc: We fear he can't be defeated, but maybe we can hold back his creatures and keep city safe.

steps.text: If the player has beaten the Inferno:

steps.npc: You, a mere JalYt, showed us he can be stopped though. Thanks to you, we still have hope.

steps.text: If the player has not yet sacrificed a fire cape:

steps.player: I like to think I'm pretty trustworthy. If you tell me, maybe I can help in some way.

steps.npc: I have one idea. If you sacrifice your fire cape to me, I can take your word.

But now you can be trusted, I must also give warning. Another being lives in the Inferno, one more powerful than any TzHaar.
We do not know where he came from. All we know is that TzKal-Zuk is hungry. Hungry for memories, memories beyond the Inferno.
We think his goal is the city itself. Lots of TzHaar memories here for him. Luckily, he is trapped in prison down there, and we are keeping him at bay by offering sacrifices.
We fear he can't be defeated, but maybe we can hold back his creatures and keep city safe.

Please accept this cape as a token of appreciation.

the-inferno-upon-defeating-tzkal-zuk.text: TzHaar-Ket-Keh hands you an Infernal cape and [16440/32880] TokKul.

upon-using-a-tzkal-slayer-helmet-on-him.npc: Impressive JalYt, but why do you show me this?

upon-using-a-tzkal-slayer-helmet-on-him.player: I have conquered the most difficult challenges across Gielinor. But I wish to challenge myself further.
I wish to challenge the Inferno on my own terms, without the endorsement of a slayer master.

upon-using-a-tzkal-slayer-helmet-on-him.npc: Hmm. You ask for much, JalYt. But if anybody has proven themselves worthy it is you.
Very well. I shall be the one to endorse your attempts to reach even greater heights.

upon-using-a-tzkal-slayer-helmet-on-him.player: Thank you TzHaar-Ket-Keh. You won't regret it.

historical-dialogue.player: Wow what has happened here? That doesn't look good!

historical-dialogue.npc: We pushed it too far! JalYt would not understand. The memories, we needed them. Now big Inferno.

steps.player: What is this place?

steps.npc: This is our birthing pool. TzHaar are born from eggs incubated in this large pool here.
When hatched, we retain memories. Memories and knowledge passed on from ancestors who returned to the lava.

steps.player: Something doesn't seem right... There's a large opening.
What happened here?

steps.npc: We went too far... way too far, we need the memories. JalYt would not understand.

steps.player: Please help me to understand then.

steps.npc: We TzHaar have special ability. When incubated in lava, a hatched TzHaar retains knowledge and memories of ancestors who returned to the lava.
Not all memories though, those about earliest ancestors were not being retained. We experiment.
We increased the depth at which the eggs are incubated. Over time this worked, newly hatched TzHaar had more memories of lost history!

steps.player: That sounds fantastic though, uncovering the past to determine where your species originated?

steps.npc: Yes, but you JalYt do not understand, we kept pushing it. We wanted answers, but too deep we went.
Eventually the pool collapsed into a sink hole, huge Inferno there. This was big ancient incubation chamber.
We decide to experiment. We take eggs from creatures in Fight Cave and incubate them.
We hatched eggs in there and it was not a good decision. They were so different, bigger, stronger and fought each other for dominance.

steps.text: If player has not yet sacrificed a fire cape:

steps.npc: Instead of knowledge, we now have a prison of dangerous TzHaar creatures - it gets worse but I cannot trust JalYt with this knowledge yet.

steps.text: If player has sacrificed a fire cape:

steps.npc: Instead of knowledge, we now have a prison of dangerous creatures... and they're not under our control.
One grew incredibly strong, powerful. He controls those creatures in the prison. TzKal-Zuk, as we call him...is hungry.
Hungry for memories, memories beyond the Inferno, which only TzHaar in the city can provide.

steps.player: Do you know what he's planning? What are you doing?

steps.npc: We can only guess one day he will want to scale up into the city himself. We are keeping him at bay by offering sacrifices for him to feast on.

steps.player: Is there no way to take him out?

steps.npc: We fear not. But we hoped you, with your fancy JalYt weaponry, would be able to help hold back his creatures. You proved your commitment by sacrificing your fire cape.

steps.player: Can I go down there?
